_comment: Example of the feature_validation section of config.json, written by references/setup.md. Placeholder values only. Don't commit a real config (it holds user ids).

pm_user.tracker_user: <value your tracker's owner field stores for you>

feature_source._comment: type: 'tracker' or 'pasted'. tracker: notion | jira | airtable | other.

fields.title: Feature
fields._comment: Map each role to your tracker's actual property name. Set a key to null if your tracker has no such property.

resolved_property_names._comment: Filled at setup by reading the tracker schema: actual_name, type, options, write_form per property.

due_rule._comment: mode: 'tracker_flags' (use due_flag / pre_change_flag), 'cadence' (Last Validated older than cadence_days, or next-phase target date today or tomorrow), or 'all' (every feature supplied is due). cadence_days: the PM's choice; setup suggests 7.

output._comment: 'markdown' (report in chat, writes nothing) or 'tracker' (writes Last Validated, Validated by, agreed Tier C edits, and an audit comment).

jira._comment: Optional; narrows search. Empty means search accessible projects by feature name.

field_source_map._comment: Which sources corroborate each high-signal field, in priority order. 'spec' = the spec link on the feature; 'conviction' = the feature's linked conviction doc; 'milestones' = related milestone target dates; 'feature_body' = the record body and notes fields (context only, not external corroboration); 'pasted' = evidence the PM pasted this run; 'jira' = the feature's linked epic or issues in the tracker (narrowed by sources.jira.project_keys); 'slack' = the channels in sources.slack_sources; 'doc:<name>' = the doc_sources entry with that name.

notify._comment: mode: 'always', 'only_if_tier_c', or 'never'. Never notifies on a nothing-due run.

schedule._comment: on_demand (default), or the frequency registered in your host (daily recommended). For reference only; the host owns the actual schedule.

calibration._comment: Tracker write-back only. When done=false, the first write-back run presents would-be Tier A validations for approval instead of writing them.
